estimand_functional: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\{T\subseteq\mathcal V:|T|=r,\ \exists t\text{ ordering }T\text{ with }Q_{tt}\succ0\text{ and }L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}\text{ diagonal and nonnegative for every }e\}\)

sampling_model.design: Independent multi-sample Gaussian covariance experiment across environments \(e\in\mathcal E\).
sampling_model.units: For each environment, \(n_e\) independent centered observations \(Y_{ei}\in\mathbb R^d\).
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown soft interventions change exactly \(r\) observed structural-noise variances; the fixed baseline is a minimum-variance condition and a designed reference environment increases every target variance.
sampling_model.overlap: Covariances obey \(mI_d\preceq\Sigma_e\preceq MI_d\); no separation from profile collisions is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The empirical covariance tuple is used directly; stationary latent confounding and measurement error cancel in population covariance differences.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 characterizes the LIT output under latent confounding as a candidate superset of the observed intervention targets.
Theorem 1 gives uniqueness of the global joint diagonalizer if and only if every pair of intervention-variance profiles is noncollinear.
The identifiability theorem recovers the unmixing matrix up to scaling and permutation when differenced diagonal profiles are pairwise noncollinear.

In arXiv v1, Theorems 1--3 establish sign-and-permutation equivalence, point identification under distinct variance-ratio eigenvalues, and the eigen-decomposition representation; Section III, Definition 4, and the later point- and set-identification subsections characterize restricted rotation sets under eigenvalue multiplicity.
Theorem 1 constructs a test-inversion confidence set for a causal effect while retaining uncertainty over two linear causal structures.
The paper constructs random sets with pointwise and uniform asymptotic coverage for an identified set and its images by objective-function inversion.
Theorems 1--2 give weak-identification-robust chi-square inference for full and selected structural parameters in heteroskedastic models.

tldr: Under a designed minimum-variance baseline and a common reference environment that increases every target variance, stationary latent confounding and measurement error disappear from covariance differences, but collisions among structural-variance profiles destroy unique global diagonalization.  The complete labeled target fiber is identified instead: a size-\(r\) set is compatible exactly when some ordering passes a positive principal-block \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) certificate, and every certificate has a legal acyclic Gaussian realization at any positive-definite baseline with strictly positive structural and measurement noises.  Explicit boundary witnesses show that signed shifts invalidate the nonnegative-diagonal test and that removing the common reference destroys the rank-\(r\) carrier.  A subset-memoized pivot recursion computes all compatible sets, while measurable feasible-point augmentation yields always-nonempty honest family regions; classification information distance gives matching consistency and impossibility regimes near profile collisions.

project_justification.gap: Unknown-target methods with latent confounding return candidate supersets, whereas covariance-difference methods recover a global mixing matrix only under profile separation.  Bacchiocchi et al. first give sign/permutation, distinct-eigenvalue, and eigen-decomposition results and later study multiplicity through restricted HSVAR rotation sets, not the complete family of observed causal target labels.
project_justification.niche: With a designed minimum-variance baseline and a common reference that changes all targets, acyclicity supplies a triangular labeling constraint that survives profile collisions and can be checked on candidate target principal blocks even when individual changed columns are not identified.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an if-and-only-if labeled-fiber theorem, an arbitrary-baseline positive-noise converse, a precise boundary result for signed shifts and split references, a complete subset recursion, and honest classification inference whose nonclosed-model selector and information boundary remain valid at covariance-profile collisions.

related_work: Yang, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash motivate the target-matching problem and show that their latent-confounded LIT output is a superset rather than the exact target set.  BACKSHIFT and coroICA provide the covariance-differencing and joint-diagonalization ancestors; their broader shift formulations motivate the method, while the nonnegative fixed-baseline and common-reference restrictions here are new panel-design conditions rather than inherited BACKSHIFT assumptions.  Yang et al. analyze measurement error after assuming a recoverable mixing matrix; here invariant positive measurement error cancels before the target fiber is characterized.  In Bacchiocchi et al., arXiv v1 Theorems 1--3 establish sign/permutation equivalence, distinct-eigenvalue point identification, and the eigen-decomposition representation.  Their multiplicity object appears later in Section III, Definition 4 and the point- and set-identification subsections: an admissible rotation set for structural parameters and impulse responses under zero and sign restrictions.  The present fiber intersects covariance-shift factorizations with unit-lower acyclicity and observed labels, producing a strictly different and more constrained discrete object rather than extending those three preliminary theorems.  Jaber et al. and Squires et al. make completeness over unknown-target equivalence classes algorithmically central under graphical oracle conditions; the present recursion uses exact covariance pivots.  Brown--Purves measurable selection and Romano--Shaikh identified-set inversion motivate the inference construction, while Lewis motivates treating near-proportional profiles as weak identification.  Wu et al. provide the concrete consumer: perturbation-target prediction under acknowledged unseen-confounder limitations, for which the proposed output is an honest effective-target family only when the narrower covariance model is defensible.
technical_internal_limitation: The model assumes environment-invariant structural coefficients, latent covariance, and measurement-error covariance, a fixed dimension, exact rank \(r\), common shift range, a designed minimum-variance baseline, and one reference environment with a positive increment at every target.  The boundary proposition shows that signed shifts invalidate the nonnegative certificate and that a panel without a common reference requires an aggregate multi-environment carrier instead of \(Q\).  If latent factors or measurement errors change with the environment, covariance differencing need not isolate observed structural-noise shifts.  The semialgebraic algorithm is a certification route, not a claim of transcriptome-scale computation, and the biological labels are effective structural-noise targets rather than direct binding sites.
honest_scope: The exact fiber, positive-noise realization, design-restriction boundary, subset recursion, measurable approximate selector, finite-sample family coverage, and two-regime information boundary are theorem targets.  The finite-sample sufficient threshold is \(\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)>2c_{\alpha}+1\) on the stated confidence event, with the full \(x\)-indexed bound retained for consistency.  The exact local minimax power envelope at bounded information distance is deliberately open.  When \(r=1\), the proposal reduces to the familiar rank-one ambiguity \(\{\{j\}:Q_{jj}>0\}\); no stronger single-target identification is claimed.

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Number of observed structural-noise coordinates whose variances change.

symbols.name: Env
symbols.def: Environment labels, with baseline environment \(0\) and reference environment \(1\).

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: A record \(\mu\) containing the invariant structural coefficients, latent loading, primitive noise laws, target labels, and environment-specific structural-variance shifts.
symbols.role: Generic member of the legal SCM class.

symbols.name: Umu
symbols.role: Maps primitive disturbances to observed variables.

symbols.name: Cmu
symbols.def: Invariant loading \(C_{\mu}\) of \(d\) stationary latent roots; zero loading columns permit fewer effective latent factors.

symbols.name: OmegaH
symbols.def: Invariant covariance \(\Omega_{H,\mu}\) of the latent roots.

symbols.name: Tmu
symbols.def: Observed coordinates whose structural-noise variances change in \(\mu\).
symbols.role: Causal target set of a model.

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.def: Variance increments \(\lambda=(\lambda_{ej}:1\le e\le E,\ j\in\mathcal V)\) relative to environment \(0\).
symbols.role: Environment profile of each observed structural noise.

symbols.name: epsilone
symbols.def: Observed structural-noise vector with covariance \(\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda_e)\), taking \(\lambda_0=0\).

symbols.name: Mscm
symbols.def: Legal fixed-dimensional Gaussian covariance-shift SCM class \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\).

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: Candidate labeled target set; its cardinality is imposed where the candidate is evaluated.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: An ordering of the elements of \(T\).

symbols.name: Pt
symbols.def: Matrix selecting the coordinates in the order \(t\).

symbols.name: Qtt
symbols.def: Ordered reference principal block \(Q_{tt}=P_t QP_t^{\mathsf T}\).

symbols.name: Lt
symbols.def: Unit-lower factor \(L_t\) in the positive \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization of \(Q_{tt}\).

symbols.name: Nmat
symbols.def: Generic symmetric matrix whose range is contained in the reference range.

symbols.name: tau
symbols.def: Noise-slack scalar chosen below the minimum-eigenvalue bound in the completion.

symbols.name: Rzero
symbols.def: Latent residual covariance \(R_0=\Sigma_0-\tau U_tU_t^{\mathsf T}-\tau I_d\).

symbols.name: Ct
symbols.def: Latent loading \(C_t=U_t^{-1}R_0^{1/2}\) used by the completion.

symbols.name: Fcausal
symbols.def: Target sets realized by models in \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\) with covariance tuple \(\theta\).

symbols.name: Falg
symbols.def: Target sets admitting at least one ordered \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) certificate.

symbols.name: Comp
symbols.role: Labels targeted in every compatible model.

symbols.name: Poss
symbols.role: Labels targeted in some compatible model.

symbols.name: PS
symbols.def: Matrix selecting the coordinates indexed by \(S\) in a fixed canonical order.

symbols.name: Pivot
symbols.def: Admissibility of a label \(j\notin S\) for the global proportionality pivot.

symbols.name: zeta
symbols.def: Generic tuple \(\zeta=(Z_0,\ldots,Z_E)\) used to define the bounded legal covariance class.

symbols.name: ThetaK
symbols.def: Bounded nonempty exact-rank legal covariance class \(\Theta_K\).

symbols.name: normw
symbols.def: Sample-size weighted Frobenius norm \(\lVert a\rVert_w^2=\sum_{e=0}^{E}n_e\lVert a_e\rVert_F^2\).

symbols.name: epsilon
symbols.def: Approximation tolerance \(\epsilon\) for projection onto the nonclosed model.

symbols.name: stilde
symbols.def: A definable-choice section \(s_{\epsilon}\) of \(G_{\epsilon}\), including a finite ordered-certificate witness.

symbols.name: Fout
symbols.def: Outer target family \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n}=\bigcup_{\zeta\in R_n\cap\Theta_K}\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\zeta)\).

symbols.name: Hpert
symbols.role: Argument of the frozen information norm.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Profile-split parameter in the four-node collision path.

symbols.def: Path \(\theta_{\gamma}\) with fixed baseline and reference shift and with \(\Delta_2(\gamma)=2aa^{\mathsf T}+(2+\gamma)bb^{\mathsf T}\), where \(a=(1,1,2,1)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(b=(0,1,1,2)^{\mathsf T}\).

symbols.name: xrad
symbols.def: Deterministic sampling-error threshold \(x\) used to control the weighted covariance error event.

symbols.def: Explicit three-node signed-shift boundary tuple \(\theta^{\pm}\) defined in \(\text{def:restriction-boundary-witnesses}\).
symbols.role: Witness for failure of the nonnegative-diagonal certificate under signed variance changes.

symbols.name: thetaSplitRef
symbols.def: Explicit three-node split-reference boundary tuple \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\) defined in \(\text{def:restriction-boundary-witnesses}\).
symbols.role: Witness for failure of the single-reference rank carrier when no environment shifts every target.

symbols.name: betastar
symbols.def: Optimal honest correct-certification probability to be derived in \(\text{oeq:local-power-envelope}\).

assumptions.condition: The observed coefficient matrix \(B_{\mu}\) is permutation-similar to a strictly lower-triangular matrix.
For every \(e\in\mathcal E\), the primitive vector \((H_e,\varepsilon_e,\eta_e)\) is centered Gaussian.
For every \(e\in\mathcal E\), the collection consisting of \(H_e\), all coordinates of \(\varepsilon_e\), and \(\eta_e\) is mutually independent.

standard.name: Independent structural noises with separate latent roots

assumptions.condition: The covariance of \(H_e\) equals \(\Omega_{H,\mu}\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\).
The covariance of \(\eta_e\) equals the same diagonal matrix \(\Omega_{\eta,\mu}\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\).

standard.name: Classical additive measurement error with invariant variance

assumptions.condition: Every coordinate of \(\omega_{0,\mu}\) is strictly positive.

novel.justification: This is a fixed-baseline-minimum design restriction.  It is satisfied when an untreated or lowest-intensity condition is fixed as baseline and every included stimulation arm can only add structural-noise variance on an effective target, as in randomized dose-escalation or activation panels.

assumptions.condition: For every \(j\in T_{\mu}\), the reference increment satisfies \(\lambda_{1j}>0\).

novel.justification: This is a common-reference panel restriction.  A designed factorial or dose panel can include one broad calibration environment whose stimulation is strong enough to increase the variance of every coordinate that changes anywhere in the panel, even when those effective coordinates are not labeled in advance.

assumptions.condition: For every \(e\in\mathcal E\), the generic tuple satisfies \(mI_d\preceq Z_e\preceq MI_d\).
There exist \(T\subseteq\mathcal V\) with \(\lvert T\rvert=r\) and an ordering \(t\) of \(T\) such that \(\operatorname{Cert}(\zeta,T,t)\) holds.
Conditional on \(\theta\), the observations \(Y_{ei}\sim N(0,\Sigma_e)\) are independent over all \(e\in\mathcal E\) and \(1\le i\le n_e\).

definitions.name: legal Gaussian covariance-shift SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}=\{\mu_{d,E,r}: B_{\mu}\text{ is acyclic};\ (H_e,\varepsilon_e,\eta_e)\text{ obey the centered Gaussian and independence conditions};\ \operatorname{Cov}(H_e)=\Omega_{H,\mu};\ \operatorname{Cov}(\eta_e)=\Omega_{\eta,\mu};\ \omega_{0,\mu}>0;\ \Omega_{\eta,\mu}\succ0;\ |T_{\mu}|=r;\ \lambda_{ej}=0\text{ off }T_{\mu};\ \lambda_{ej}\ge0\text{ on }T_{\mu};\ \lambda_{1j}>0\text{ on }T_{\mu}\}\).

definitions.name: ordered LDL certificate
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\iff [\,t\text{ orders }T,\ Q_{tt}\succ0,\ Q_{tt}=L_tD_tL_t^{\mathsf T},\ L_t\text{ unit lower triangular},\ D_t\text{ diagonal positive},\ \Lambda_{e,t}=L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}\text{ diagonal and entrywise nonnegative for every }1\le e\le E\,]\).

definitions.name: causal target fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\{T\subseteq\mathcal V:|T|=r,\ \exists\mu\in\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\text{ with }T_{\mu}=T\text{ and }\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu}(Y_e)=\Sigma_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E\}\).

definitions.name: positive-noise SCM completion
definitions.construction: Given \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\), set \(W_t=QP_t^{\mathsf T}Q_{tt}^{-1}\), \(A_t=W_tL_t\), \(U_t=\begin{psmallmatrix}L_t&0\\A_{t,T^c}&I_{d-r}\end{psmallmatrix}\) after placing \(t\) first, \(B_t=I_d-U_t^{-1}\), choose \(0<\tau<\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_0)/(2(\lVert U_t\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2+1))\), set \(R_0=\Sigma_0-\tau U_tU_t^{\mathsf T}-\tau I_d\), set \(C_t=U_t^{-1}R_0^{1/2}\), take \(H_e\sim N(0,I_d)\), baseline structural and measurement covariances \(\tau I_d\), and target increments \(\operatorname{diag}(\Lambda_{e,t})\) on \(t\) with zero increments off \(T\).

definitions.name: subset-memoized global pivot recursion
definitions.construction: Initialize \(S=\varnothing\), \(R_S=Q\), and \(M_{e,S}=\Delta_e\).  A label \(j\notin S\) is admissible when \(q=(R_S)_{jj}>0\), \(m_e=(M_{e,S})_{jj}\ge0\), and \(q(M_{e,S})_{:j}=m_e(R_S)_{:j}\) for every \(1\le e\le E\); with \(u=(R_S)_{:j}/q\), update \(R_{S\cup\{j\}}=R_S-quu^{\mathsf T}\) and \(M_{e,S\cup\{j\}}=M_{e,S}-m_euu^{\mathsf T}\), memoizing only \(S\cup\{j\}\).

definitions.name: compulsory-and-possible classification
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C(\theta)=\bigcap_{T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)}T\), \(\mathcal P(\theta)=\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)}T\), and \(h(\theta)=(\mathcal C(\theta),\mathcal P(\theta))\).

definitions.name: bounded legal covariance class
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_K=\{\zeta_{d,E,r}:mI_d\preceq Z_e\preceq MI_d\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E;\ \operatorname{rank}(Z_1-Z_0)=r;\ \operatorname{range}(Z_e-Z_0)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Z_1-Z_0)\text{ for every }1\le e\le E;\ \exists T,t\text{ with }|T|=r\text{ and }\operatorname{Cert}(\zeta,T,t)\}\).

definitions.name: certified approximate covariance selector
definitions.construction: Fix a cylindrical algebraic decomposition of the semialgebraic graph \(G_{\epsilon}\) together with its ordered-certificate witness variables, and let \(s_{\epsilon}(s)\) be the definable-choice section obtained by taking the first nonempty cell in that fixed decomposition.

definitions.name: augmented target-family confidence region
definitions.construction: \(W_n=\{\zeta:mI_d\preceq Z_e\preceq MI_d,\ \lVert\zeta-\widehat\Sigma\rVert_w\le c_{\alpha}\}\), \(\widetilde\theta_n=s_1(\widehat\Sigma)\), \(R_n=W_n\cup\{\widetilde\theta_n\}\), \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n}=\bigcup_{\zeta\in R_n\cap\Theta_K}\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\zeta)\), and \(\mathcal H_n=\{h(\zeta):\zeta\in R_n\cap\Theta_K\}\).

definitions.name: four-node profile-collision path
definitions.construction: For \(d=4\), \(r=2\), and \(E=2\), take \(a=(1,1,2,1)^{\mathsf T}\), \(b=(0,1,1,2)^{\mathsf T}\), \(Q=aa^{\mathsf T}+bb^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\Delta_2(\gamma)=2aa^{\mathsf T}+(2+\gamma)bb^{\mathsf T}\), with the fixed positive-definite baseline given by the positive-noise completion.

definitions.name: signed-shift and split-reference boundary witnesses
definitions.construction: For \(d=3\), \(r=2\), and \(E=2\), set \(B_{\mu}=0\), \(C_{\mu}=0\), \(\omega_{0,\mu}=(3/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T}\), \(\Omega_{\eta,\mu}=I_3/2\), and \(T_{\mu}=\{1,2\}\).  Define \(\theta^{\pm}\) by \(\lambda_1=(1,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\lambda_2=(-1/2,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\), so \(\Sigma_0=2I_3\), \(\Sigma_1=\operatorname{diag}(3,3,2)\), and \(\Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(3/2,2,2)\).  Define \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\) by \(\lambda_1=(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\lambda_2=(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\), so \(\Sigma_0=2I_3\), \(\Sigma_1=\operatorname{diag}(3,2,2)\), and \(\Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(2,3,2)\).

definitions.name: local collision power-envelope handle
definitions.construction: Construct factorization-preserving local paths in each semialgebraic classification stratum through a profile collision, derive their Gaussian covariance local asymptotic normal experiment in the norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{I,n,\theta}\), and reduce optimal honest certification of \(h(\theta)\) to testing the resulting finite union of tangent cones in order to determine \(\beta^{\star}(c)\).

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\), \(Q_{tt}\) is invertible, \(W_t=QP_t^{\mathsf T}Q_{tt}^{-1}\), and \(N=N^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{range}(N)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)\), then \(N=W_t(P_tNP_t^{\mathsf T})W_t^{\mathsf T}\).
statements.justification: The lemma upgrades target-block diagonalization to an identity for every full covariance shift.
statements.gap: BACKSHIFT and coroICA use global diagonalizers; neither isolates the coordinate-restriction inverse needed for a labeled principal-block converse.
statements.consumer: The positive-noise realization theorem uses this identity to reconstruct every full shift from its target block.

statements.statement: For every \(T\subseteq\mathcal V\) and ordering \(t\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\), the construction in \(\text{def:positive-noise-completion}\) yields a model in \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\) with target set \(T\), covariance \(\operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)=\Sigma_e\) for all \(e\in\mathcal E\), strictly positive baseline structural-noise variances, and strictly positive stationary measurement-error variances.
statements.justification: A covariance certificate is causally meaningful only if every certified label set has a legal SCM witness with positive noise.
statements.gap: Yang et al. begin from a separately recovered mixing matrix, and measurement-error identification begins from separability; neither proves arbitrary-baseline realization from covariance shifts alone.
statements.consumer: The construction lets an applied analyst interpret every reported target set as a realizable alternative causal explanation rather than an algebraic artifact.

statements.statement: For every covariance tuple \(\theta\) satisfying \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\), and \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)\) for all \(1\le e\le E\), \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\).  Equivalently, a labeled size-\(r\) set is compatible if and only if some ordering has a positive-definite reference principal block whose unique unit-lower \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factor simultaneously transforms every target-block shift to a diagonal entrywise-nonnegative matrix.
statements.justification: This is the necessary-and-sufficient population kernel that replaces nonsharp target supersets by the complete labeled fiber.
statements.gap: Yang, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash characterize a superset under latent confounding, while BACKSHIFT and coroICA identify a global mixing matrix only when variance profiles separate; none characterizes all labeled acyclic target sets at profile collisions.
statements.consumer: Unknown-target perturbation studies can report all and only covariance-compatible effective target sets while retaining stationary latent confounding and measurement error.

statements.statement: The leaves of depth \(r\) accepted by the recursion in \(\text{def:subset-pivot-recursion}\) are exactly \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\).  Every reached residual pair \((R_S,(M_{e,S})_{e=1}^{E})\) depends only on \(S\), so the algorithm terminates after visiting at most \(\sum_{k=0}^{r}\binom{d}{k}\) subset states, and the intersection and union of its leaves equal \(\mathcal C(\theta)\) and \(\mathcal P(\theta)\).
statements.justification: The theorem turns the characterization into a terminating complete-class algorithm without enumerating DAGs or repeated order prefixes.
statements.gap: Jaber et al. and Squires et al. give complete graphical or permutation procedures under different oracle models; the covariance-shift literature has no subset-memoized triangular pivot certificate for the complete labeled fiber.
statements.consumer: The algorithm produces compulsory and possible effective targets for small perturbation panels and supplies witness orderings for every reported set.

statements.statement: For every \(\epsilon>0\), the correspondence \(G_{\epsilon}\) admits a semialgebraic, hence Borel measurable, section \(s_{\epsilon}\) that returns both \(s_{\epsilon}(s)\in\Theta_K\) and an ordered certificate witness, with \(\lVert s_{\epsilon}(s)-s\rVert_w<\inf_{\zeta\in\Theta_K}\lVert\zeta-s\rVert_w+\epsilon\) for every covariance statistic \(s\).
statements.justification: This closes the nonattainment gap created by exact rank and strict positive pivots without assuming a nearest model point exists.
statements.gap: Brown and Purves treat measurable attained extrema, and Romano and Shaikh invert criteria over identified sets; neither supplies certified approximate projection through this nonclosed exact-rank semialgebraic covariance model.
statements.consumer: The augmented confidence construction needs this selector to be measurable and nonempty on every sample, including off-model empirical covariances.

statements.statement: Under the independent Gaussian sampling design, uniformly over \(\theta\in\Theta_K\), \(\Pr_{\theta}[\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n}\text{ and }h(\theta)\in\mathcal H_n]\ge1-\alpha\).  The region \(R_n\cap\Theta_K\) is nonempty for every sample, and a rule reports a classification only when \(\mathcal H_n\) is a singleton has probability at most \(\alpha\) of reporting a classification different from \(h(\theta)\).
statements.justification: Family coverage must retain structural uncertainty and remain well-defined when the raw covariance region misses the nonclosed model.
statements.gap: Strieder et al. retain graph uncertainty by test inversion and Romano--Shaikh cover identified sets, but neither gives always-nonempty coverage of a discontinuous discrete target family under exact-rank covariance restrictions.
statements.consumer: A Perturb-seq or Sci-Plex audit can abstain near collisions while maintaining finite-sample coverage of all effective target explanations under the stated covariance model.

statements.statement: For every \(x>0\), on the event \(\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w\le x\), every point of \(R_n\) is within weighted distance strictly less than \(\max\{x+c_{\alpha},2x+1\}\) of \(\theta\).  Hence, if \(\max\{x+c_{\alpha},2x+1\}<\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)\), the singleton rule based on \(\mathcal H_n\) reports \(h(\theta)\), and its failure probability is at most \(V_{\max}/x^2\).  In particular, \(\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)>2c_{\alpha}+1\) implies correct reporting with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).  For every sequence \(\theta_n\in\Theta_K\) with \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\to\infty\), the rule reports \(h(\theta_n)\) with probability tending to one, uniformly over subclasses on which the infimum of \(\delta_n\) diverges.
statements.justification: The result identifies the observable separation scale at which honest abstention disappears.
statements.gap: Lewis studies weak heteroskedastic identification for continuous structural parameters; the present boundary concerns the entire discrete compulsory-and-possible target classification over a nonclosed causal fiber.
statements.consumer: Analysts obtain a diagnostic for when an exact target classification, rather than an outer family, is statistically defensible.

statements.statement: The tuple \(\theta^{\pm}\) is generated by an acyclic positive-structural-noise, positive-measurement-noise Gaussian SCM satisfying every member condition of \(\mathcal M_{3,2,2}\) except nonnegative variance shifts, with true target set \(\{1,2\}\); its transformed second target block is \(\operatorname{diag}(-1/2,0)\), so the entrywise-nonnegative ordered certificate rejects that true target.  The tuple \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\) satisfies every member condition except the common-reference restriction, with true target set \(\{1,2\}\), but its reference shift has rank one and no size-two reference principal block is positive definite.  Thus signed shifts destroy the nonnegative-diagonal necessity, while absence of a common reference destroys the rank-\(r\) carrier and the range-reconstruction step; an extension would require, respectively, baseline-variance feasibility inequalities or an aggregate carrier built from several environments.
statements.justification: The result identifies exactly which parts of the certificate fail when either design restriction is removed.
statements.gap: BACKSHIFT permits signed covariance changes and does not require a designated common reference, whereas the labeled principal-block fiber uses both restrictions; the explicit witnesses prevent that narrower result from being advertised as a general covariance-shift characterization.
statements.consumer: Panel designers learn whether to add a lowest-variance baseline and a broad calibration environment, and analysts without them know which certificate component must be replaced rather than trusted.

statements.statement: Fix \(C<\infty\).  For any possibly abstaining rule whose probability of an incorrect classification is uniformly at most \(\alpha\) on \(\Theta_K\), there exists \(\kappa=\kappa(C,\alpha,m,M,d,E)>0\) such that along every sequence \(\theta_n\in\Theta_K\) with \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\le C\), the probability of correctly certifying \(h(\theta_n)\) is at most \(1-\kappa\).
statements.justification: A matching impossibility result makes information distance a genuine certification boundary rather than only a sufficient margin.
statements.gap: Weak-heteroskedasticity tests and repeated-eigenvalue analyses do not construct opposite labeled causal-target strata while preserving acyclicity, stationary confounding, measurement error, range inclusion, and positive noises.
statements.consumer: The bound prevents overconfident effective-target declarations when covariance profiles are statistically indistinguishable.

statements.statement: Along the legal path \(\theta_{\gamma}\), \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta_{\gamma})=\{\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{1,4\}\}\) and \(h(\theta_{\gamma})=(\{1\},\{1,2,3,4\})\) for \(\gamma\ne0\), whereas at \(\gamma=0\) all six two-element target sets are compatible and \(h(\theta_0)=(\varnothing,\{1,2,3,4\})\).  For equal environment sample sizes, there exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c\sqrt n|\gamma|\le\delta_n(\theta_{\gamma})\le C\sqrt n|\gamma|\) for all sufficiently small nonzero \(\gamma\).
statements.justification: The witness proves that profile collision changes compulsory labels and that the abstract information distance has a concrete first-order scale.
statements.gap: Bacchiocchi et al. study rotation sets at repeated HSVAR eigenvalues, but not a legal acyclic SCM path whose complete labeled target family changes with a computed Gaussian-information rate.
statements.consumer: The example is an early kill test for implementations of augmentation, classification, and pivot memoization in the smallest nontrivial case.

statements.statement: When \(r=1\) and \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\ne\varnothing\), the sharp fiber reduces to \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\{\{j\}:Q_{jj}>0\}\).
statements.justification: This reduction checks that the multivariate certificate collapses to the known rank-one changing-column ambiguity.
statements.gap: The rank-one case is implicit in covariance-factor arguments, but is stated here as the required sanity reduction of the general labeled-fiber theorem.
statements.consumer: Practitioners with single effective perturbations obtain a closed-form candidate list without running the recursion.

statements.statement: Can the handle in \(\text{def:power-envelope-handle}\) derive the limiting minimax correct-certification envelope \(\beta^{\star}(c)\) for uniformly \(\alpha\)-honest classifiers along every regular sequence with \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\to c\in(0,\infty)\), and construct a classifier attaining that envelope uniformly over the corresponding semialgebraic tangent-cone experiment?
statements.justification: The current upper and lower results locate the consistency boundary but do not determine optimal finite local power at the boundary.
statements.gap: Andrews--Cheng organize drifting identification regimes and Lewis gives robust tests, but neither derives a decision envelope for a finite-valued causal target fiber with intersecting semialgebraic strata.
statements.consumer: A solved envelope would calibrate how often an honest perturbation-target procedure should certify rather than abstain at a scientifically meaningful near-collision.
